decisions.mark: explains that a code carries TWO layers — a high-level module part and a low-level part — and that mbedtls_strerror renders both, joined, when both are present
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80`. If it is nonzero, `mbedtls_high_level_strerr()` (`library/error.c:174`) looks it up. ... The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80`. If it is nonzero, `mbedtls_low_level_strerr()` (`library/error.c:537`) looks it up. If both parts are present, the strings are joined with `" : "`. | WHY: The answer describes the high-level and low-level parts of the code and says that `mbedtls_strerror` joins both strings with " : " when both are present.
